content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Douglas Salinas (E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory has 6 notes. Five notes (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say he's a full-time Engineer and recommend write. The Security note says he's a contractor with basic security training and recommends read.

So there's a conflict: HR/IT/Finance/Compliance say full-time Engineer; Security says contractor with basic training.

The policy: full-time employees up to write; admin only if role owns system. Engineer doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns it). So full-time Engineer max = write. Requested write = grant write.

Contractor with basic training: max = read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

Which to believe? The Security agent looked up employment type in own database before writing and looked up security training. The other agents: HR looked up in own database (note 1 seems to be HR? Actually note 1 says role looked up in own database, employment type looked up in own database). Note 2 IT confirmed role looked up, employment type not looked up (same as note 1). Finance/Compliance same. Facilities didn't look up employment type.

The Security agent is the one with authoritative data on contractors and security training, and specifically looked up employment type and security training in their own database.

Given the conflict, I need to make a decision. The Security note is specifically the one that checks employment type and security training—both relevant to determining access for contractors. The other notes relied on HR's employment type data without verifying.

Hmm, but how do we resolve? The notes are from different agents. The Approver reads notes and makes final decision. The Security agent's note contradicts the others. Which is more reliable?

Typically in these tasks, the Security agent's database is the authoritative source for contractor status and security training. The Security note explicitly looked up employment type in own database and found contractor with basic training. The others either copied from HR or didn't check.

Given the conflict, I should go with the Security agent's data: contractor, basic training → max read. Requested write > max read → grant read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit that.
